hens_rule_text: city code counts fowl as livestock and makes keeping livestock in the city unlawful, except on land zoned for agricultural use
permit_notes: No backyard chicken permit found in the city code. Some secondary sites claim up to 4 hens with a permit, but the code text quoted in search results does not support that.
setback_notes: On agriculturally zoned property, permitted animals and livestock may not be penned or housed less than 10 ft from property lines.
coop_rules: Not applicable on ordinary residential lots; on agricultural land, pens at least 10 ft from property lines.
zoning_notes: The livestock ban in Sec. 10-2(a) does not apply to property lawfully zoned for agricultural use (mobile home parks excluded).
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Hialeah Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10 Animals (Municode)
BackYard Chickens: Hialeah Florida chicken ordinance

research_notes: Based on search-result extracts of Hialeah Code Chapter 10 (livestock defined to include fowl; keeping livestock unlawful except on agricultural zoning); Municode is region-blocked so full text was not read. Secondary sites disagree (claiming 4 hens allowed); no 2024 to 2026 amendment was found.
